metric.why: Annual matching and hourly matching are very different claims; hourly carbon-free matching is the harder standard the largest operators now report progress against. Reading which claim is being made matters more than the percentage.
metric.definition: The share of facility consumption matched by renewable generation, reported either as annual matching through purchased certificates or as around-the-clock hourly matching.

reading.body:
The standard used to measure renewable energy at data centers—whether annual or hourly matching—matters more than the percentage itself, because hourly matching is substantially harder to achieve than buying annual certificates.

Large data center operators now compete on hourly carbon-free matching, a claim that requires renewable generation aligned to consumption in real time rather than balanced across a full year. Annual matching through purchased certificates is easier to claim but does not constrain when electricity actually comes from the grid. For AI infrastructure, this distinction directly affects grid load patterns, since hourly matching requires either on-site generation, battery storage, or coordination with renewable plants that operate when the facility draws power.

The metric tracks sustainability reporting but does not measure total emissions or grid impact. A facility with high hourly renewable matching still consumes vast amounts of power. It also does not cover embodied carbon in construction, water use, or cooling efficiency, which are tracked separately. Reading the fine print—which matching standard is being claimed—reveals whether a data center operator is making a harder engineering commitment or a looser financial one.
